page.overview:
What is Brandywine Bridge?

The Brandywine Bridge, originally called the Bridge of Stonebows, allowed the East-West Road to cross the Brandywine River in The Shire.

The only other crossings of the Brandywine within the Shire were at Bucklebury Ferry and Sarn Ford.

The bridge was built some time before TA 1601 either by the Dúnedain of Arnor or the Dwarves. King Argeleb II allowed the Hobbits migrating from the Vales of Anduin to settle in the Shire, as long as they kept the bridge in good repair and sped his messengers on their way.

On their journey to Bree in TA 3018, Frodo, Sam and Pippin did not take the bridge, for the Black Riders were thought to be looking on the Great East Road for Frodo and the One Ring. The Hobbits did, however, attempt to use the bridge on their return journey the following year, but found it barricaded with spiked gates.
